artifacts.description: feat(kernel): fillet and chamfer on edges by index

acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::fillet(&self, s, edges: &[SubShape], radius: f64) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>` and `Kernel::chamfer(&self, s, edges: &[SubShape], distance: f64) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented and implemented for `OcctKernel`. Duplicate edges in the list are treated as one. New shim functions are `noexcept` and catch C++ exceptions; every new `unsafe` call is in `ffi` with a SAFETY comment.

Box tests on `make_box((0,0,0),(10,20,30))` (volume 6000; edges of length 10, 20 and 30, four of each). Volumes within 1e-6 relative: per-edge fillet r=2 removes (4 − π)·L, 7/15/10; per-edge chamfer d=2 removes 2·L, 7/15/10; two opposite edges fillet r=2: 8 faces and the sum of both removals; bounding box unchanged.

Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput` and checked before anything reaches OCCT: radius or distance ≤ 0 or not finite; an empty edge list; a `SubShape` whose kind isn't `Edge`; an edge index out of range.
A radius OCCT can't build (radius 15 on any edge of the box) returns an `Err` (not `Ok`, not a panic), and the input shape is still usable afterwards (its volume is still 6000).
No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
